Content:
For example, suppose we want to calculate the sum of the infinite geometric series
[MATH: 3 + 1 + \dfrac 1 3 + \dfrac 1 9 + \dfrac{1}{27} + \cdots\,.]

sections.normalized_html: Calculate the sum to infinity of the geometric series [MATH: 1 - \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{16} - \dfrac{1}{64} + \dots .]
sections.readable_text: Calculate the sum to infinity of the geometric series [MATH: 1 - \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{16} - \dfrac{1}{64} + \dots .]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
The sum to infinity [MATH: S_\infty] of a geometric series is given by the formula

[MATH: S_\infty = \dfrac{a_1}{1-r}, \qquad |r| < 1,]

where [MATH: a_1] is the first term and [MATH: r] is the common ratio.

For the given geometric series, the first term is [MATH: a_1 = 1] and the common ratio is

[MATH: r = \dfrac{a_2}{a_1} = \frac{\left(-\dfrac{1}{4}\right)}{1} = - \dfrac{1}{4}.]

So, using the formula, we find that the sum to infinity is

[MATH: S_{∞}|= (a_{1})/(1 − r); = (1)/(1 − (− (1)/(4))); = (1)/(((5)/(4))); = (4)/(5).]
